newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris, Armenians clash along border.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, Armenians clash along border.

text.p: Azerbaijan and Armenia on Monday traded accusations of new cross-border attacks, the worst outburst of violence between the Transcaucasus neighbours and foes in nearly three years.

The Azeri Defence Ministry said Armenian troops had shelled Azeri positions on the northwestern part of the border late on Sunday. "The fire from light weapons continued for 10 minutes before Azeri forces returned fire and silenced the adversary," a ministry statement said.

Russia's Interfax news agency quoted the Armenian Defence Ministry as denying there had been unprovoked attacks along the heavily fortified frontier and accusing the Azeris of launching cross-border attacks.
The Armenian Defence Ministry said Azeris shelled Armenian positions for 1-1/2 hours on Sunday. It said clashes also took place at the weekend along the southern sector of the border.
The sporadic clashes over the last two weeks are the worst since a 1994 ceasefire ended a protracted territorial dispute over mountainous Nagorno-Karabakh.
Predominantly Armenian-populated Karabakh broke away from Azerbaijan in the late 1980s and thousands of people died in years of fighting over the region.
More than 20 percent of Azerbaijan's territory, including Karabakh, is now controlled by separatist forces. Baku says this amounts to occupation of its territory by Armenia proper.

Armenia says it was not a formal party in the conflict between Azerbaijan and Karabakh, but it has given its ethnic kin strong moral and military support and Karabakh leader Robert Kocharyan is now the Armenian prime minister.
Interfax said Armenia's President Levon Ter-Petrosyan and Azeri leader Haydar Aliyev had discussed the latest fighting by telephone on Friday.
Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to the ceasefire and ordered their troops to "obey it very strictly", it said.
